newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - BP signs $1 bln gas deal with Ruhrgas. [CORRECTED 17:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - BP signs $1 bln gas deal with Ruhrgas. [CORRECTED 17:00 GMT]

text.p: British Petroleum Co Plc (BP) said on Monday it signed a $1 billion, 15-year contract to supply gas to Germany's Ruhrgas in a move to help establish BP as a major European gas player.

BP will start deliveries to Ruhrgas from its British offshore fields on October 1 next year through a new link between Britain and mainland Europe when construction of the 240 km (149 miles) long Interconnector pipeline has been completed.
Industry watchers welcomed the deal, saying it was a further step for BP, which holds 25.5 percent of distributor Ruhrgas, to become a major gas operator on the continent.
Shares in BP were up one penny at 714-1/2 pence in late morning trade.

The Interconnector, in which BP has a 10 percent holding (corrects from 40 percent holding), runs from Bacton in east England to Zeebrugge in Belgium. BP will supply Ruhrgas with 15 billion cubic metres (bcm) (530 billion cu ft) of gas.

"This is a landmark gas supply deal as it represents our first sale into continental Europe from the UK and our first use of the capacity we own in the Interconnector pipeline," BP Exploration chief executive Rodney Chase said.

Similar deals to pump British gas via the Interconnector to the continent were concluded last year between distributor Wingas, a joint venture between Germany's Wintershall and Russia's Gazprom, and producers British Gas Plc and Conoco, part of U.S. group DuPont Co.

Such deals may ease downward pressure on gas prices here following oversupply since the British market for big industrial users was opened up to competition in the early 1990s, industry analysts said.
BP said its share in this market had more than doubled to 15 percent since the restructuring of its marketing activities in August 1996.
It said its combined sales of gas to industry, commerce, the power sector and the spot market placed it second to British Gas in the gas market here.
The long-term contract with Rurhrgas may not make a major contribution to BP's overall results but it is a further step towards getting a firm foothold on the continent, analysts said.
"It is going in the right direction (in the UK)...and they are becoming an important player in Europe," said analyst Jurjen Lunshof at Credit Lyonnais Laing.
